steps.title: Yeast culture and harvest
steps.instruction: Day 0: inoculate a single colony into 50 mL YPD in a 250 mL baffled flask and grow overnight to saturation. Day 1: dilute the overnight culture into 400 mL YPD at OD₆₀₀ = 0.05 in a 2 L baffled flask; grow until OD₆₀₀ = 0.5‑0.6. Harvest by rapid filtration: pour YPD onto the filter, then pour the culture down the side of the filtration vessel avoiding foam. As the last liquid passes, remove the clamp and top of the filter unit within 5 s, scrape cells gently with a pre‑chilled cell lifter, and submerge the filter into a conical tube containing liquid nitrogen (LN₂). Leave the cap loosely tightened and place the tube at –80 °C. Lyse cells by grinding: pre‑chill a mortar and pestle with LN₂ for 2‑3 min, pour out residual LN₂, add the frozen cell pellet, add 1‑5 mL LN₂, grind until LN₂ boils off, then grind the dry powder for an additional 1‑2 min. Resuspend the powder in LN₂, pour back into the original conical tube, and store at –80 °C with the cap loosely tightened. This point is a pause before gradient preparation.

steps.title: Mammalian cell culture and harvest
steps.instruction: Plate the desired number of cells in 6‑well plates, 10‑cm dishes, or 15‑cm dishes (10⁶‑10⁷ cells per dish) on Day 0. On Day 1 add cycloheximide to the media to a final concentration of 100 µg/mL and incubate 10 min at 37 °C (optional but recommended; also add cycloheximide to PBS and lysis buffer later). Pre‑chill PBS and lysis buffer on ice. Transfer the dish to an ice bucket, aspirate media, wash twice with 10 mL ice‑cold PBS, then scrape cells quickly into 5 mL ice‑cold PBS. Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL conical tube, centrifuge 5 min at 4 °C, 500 × g, discard supernatant, flash‑freeze the pellet and store at –80 °C. Proceed to gradient preparation.

steps.title: Mammalian tissue harvest and grinding
steps.instruction: Day 0: dissect a whole tissue sample, wash briefly with ice‑cold PBS, and freeze in liquid nitrogen. Day 1: pre‑chill mortar and pestle with LN₂ for 2‑3 min, pour out residual LN₂, add the frozen tissue, add 1‑5 mL LN₂, grind until LN₂ boils off, then grind the dry powder for an additional 1‑2 min. Resuspend the powder in LN₂, pour back into the original conical tube, and store at –80 °C with the cap loosely tightened. This is a pause point before gradient preparation.

steps.title: Yeast lysate preparation
steps.instruction: All steps on ice or in a 4 °C cold room. Thaw the ground yeast powder on ice for 5 min (do not add lysis buffer yet). Pre‑label four siliconized 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tubes per sample as ‘Resuspended powder’, ‘Clarified undiluted lysate’, ‘Clarified diluted lysate’, and ‘Aliquoted lysate’; also label three 0.6 mL tubes containing 90 µL ddH₂O each. Add 1 mL freshly prepared lysis buffer to the powder in each conical tube, swirl, then fully resuspend by pipetting with a P1000. Transfer the entire contents to the ‘Resuspended powder’ tubes, spin 10 min at 1 300 × g, 4 °C. Transfer the clarified lysate (~800 µL, translucent white/yellow) to the ‘Clarified undiluted’ tubes. Measure RNA by adding 10 µL lysate to 90 µL water (blank: 10 µL lysis buffer + 90 µL water) on a NanoDrop; Triton X‑100 interferes, so dilute. Dilute all lysates to 25 OD₂₆₀ U/mL (≈1 µg/µL RNA) with lysis buffer, re‑measure to ensure ≤5 % variation. Spike in uncapped Luciferase RNA to a final concentration of 100 ng/mL. Aliquot 150 µL into 1.7 mL tubes and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Mammalian cell lysate preparation
steps.instruction: Thaw the frozen cell pellet on ice. Resuspend in 100 µL lysis buffer per 10⁶ cells, transfer to a 1.7 mL tube, and incubate 10 min on ice while mixing by pipetting. (Lysis time and detergent concentration may need optimisation; Triton X‑100 can be replaced by NP‑40 or mechanical dounce homogenisation.) Centrifuge 10 min at 4 °C, 12 000 × g. Transfer the clarified lysate to a ‘Clarified undiluted’ tube. Dilute 10 µL lysate into 90 µL water and measure RNA on a NanoDrop. Dilute all samples to a final concentration of ≈20‑100 µg/mL (adjust with lysis buffer) and verify ≤5 % variation. Spike in uncapped Luciferase RNA to 100 ng/mL. Aliquot 200‑500 µL into 1.7 mL tubes; store remaining lysate (input) at –80 °C.

steps.title: Tissue lysate preparation
steps.instruction: Weigh 50 mg frozen tissue powder into LN₂‑chilled 5 mL Eppendorf tubes; work quickly to avoid warming. Dip tubes into LN₂ and shake frequently to keep powder frozen. Thaw on ice to 4 °C, then add 50‑100 µL lysis buffer per mg of powder. Pipette up/down, vortex vigorously, and let sit on ice. Allow Triton X‑100 to lyse lipids for 5‑10 min, vortex again, then spin 750 × g for 10 min at 4 °C. Transfer supernatant, then spin 12 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C. Carefully collect the middle 75 % of the clarified lysate (avoid top lipid layer and bottom debris). Take 10 µL of this supernatant into 90 µL water for NanoDrop measurement. Dilute all samples to 100 ng/µL RNA in lysis buffer containing Heparin. Spike in uncapped Luciferase RNA to 100 ng/mL, vortex, aliquot 250 µL into 1.7 mL tubes, and store remaining lysate (input) at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare sucrose gradients
steps.instruction: Perform at room temperature before lysate clarification. Aliquot 40 mL of pre‑filtered 10 % sucrose solution (stored at 4 °C) into a conical tube and let warm to RT; add DTT, cycloheximide, and Superase‑IN, then mix by gentle rotation. Prepare lysis buffer on ice (4 °C). Mark Polyclear centrifuge tubes using the SW41 Ti marker block (draw a line at the top marker). Using a stripette, fill each tube with 10 % sucrose up to ~2 mm above the line. Fill a 50 mL syringe with 50 % sucrose, expel air with the cannula pointing up, then insert the cannula vertically into the bottom of the tube (avoid mixing the two layers). Slowly dispense 50 % sucrose while keeping the cannula ~5 mm below the meniscus; stop when the interphase meniscus reaches the marked line and withdraw the cannula. Cap each tube, remove any residual sucrose with a P1000, and place tubes in the gradient‑maker holder (pre‑leveled). Run the gradient‑maker software program “14S short 10‑50 %” (30‑60 min incubation). Transfer tubes to the cold room (caps remain on) and turn on the ultracentrifuge to pre‑cool to 4 °C.

steps.title: Load lysate onto gradients and ultracentrifuge
steps.instruction: Working on ice, gently remove caps from the 10‑50 % sucrose gradients and slide tubes into SW41 Ti rotor buckets. Remove (X + 100) µL from the top of each gradient, where X is the volume of lysate you will load (typically 100 µL, up to 600 µL). Note: downstream RNA analysis works best with <100 µg lysate (≈A₂₆₀ units). Slowly layer 100‑600 µL lysate on top of the gradient, forming a neat visible layer. Save at least 10 µL of lysate as an ‘Input’ fraction for later qRT‑PCR. Weigh each tube and, if necessary, adjust weight with lysis buffer to balance. Arrange bucket pairs opposite each other (1‑4, 2‑5, 3‑6), cap the buckets, and attach to the SW41 Ti rotor. Lower the rotor, spin by hand to verify connections, then set centrifuge: vacuum ON, temperature 4 °C, speed 36 000 rpm (≈160 000 × g at r_av), time 2.5 h, acceleration 1, deceleration 7. Start the run; the instrument may pause acceleration at 3 000 rpm until vacuum is fully engaged.

steps.title: Fractionate gradients
steps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer’s Biocomp instructions (contact local representative for tutorial). While the spin is running, turn on the Bio‑Rad Econo UV monitor, allow it to warm up ≥2 h, and pre‑label 16 screw‑cap 2 mL tubes per gradient; cover with cling film or Parafilm and keep at 4 °C. Also turn on the Gilson fraction collector, Biocomp gradient station, computer, and open “Gradient Profiler V2” software. Set the zero UV reading with clean water and verify a stable baseline. After centrifugation, remove the rotor, place tubes on a rack in the cold room (do not remove caps until fractionation). Fractionate each gradient into the pre‑labeled 2 mL tubes using the following settings: speed 0.30 mm/s, total distance 75 mm, 15 fractions (distance per fraction 5.00 mm, volume per fraction 0.71 mL). Store fractions on ice, then flash‑freeze and keep at –80 °C. If the Econo‑UV monitor light turns red, pull up the piston, release the air valve, and re‑zero with water.

steps.title: DNase treatment and spike‑in
steps.instruction: Thaw all fraction tubes, input tubes, and Cells‑to‑Ct stop solution. Dilute each input sample 30‑fold by adding 6 µL input to 174 µL RNase‑free water; keep on ice. Prepare a master mix per sample: 9.9 µL Cells‑to‑Ct lysis buffer, 0.1 µL Cells‑to‑Ct DNase, 0.1 µL XenoRNA (control). For each gradient, set up 16 PCR tubes (15 fractions + input) with 10.1 µL master mix each. Add 1 µL of the corresponding fraction (or input) directly into the master mix (do not add to tube wall), pipette up/down 2‑3 times, invert gently, spin briefly, and incubate at room temperature for 5 min. Then add 1 µL Cells‑to‑Ct stop solution directly to each tube, invert, spin, and incubate at room temperature for 2 min before returning tubes to ice.

steps.title: Reverse transcription
steps.instruction: Prepare RT master mix per sample: 5 µL 2× Cells‑to‑Ct RT buffer, 0.5 µL 20× Cells‑to‑Ct RT enzyme mix (total 5.5 µL). Distribute 5.5 µL RT master mix to each PCR tube, then add 4.5 µL of the lysate (from the DNase step). Run the RT reaction in a thermocycler: 37 °C for 1 h, 95 °C for 5 min, then hold at 4 °C indefinitely. Dilute each completed RT reaction with 50 µL water, mix thoroughly, and store at –20 °C or proceed directly to qPCR.

steps.title: Quantitative real‑time PCR
steps.instruction: Set up technical duplicates for each fraction and each probe. Prepare the TaqMan PCR cocktail per reaction: 5 µL 2× TaqMan Gene Expression Master Mix + 0.5 µL 20× TaqMan assay (gene‑specific, including XenoRNA and Luciferase controls). Swirl the master mix bottle, vortex the assay stock briefly, and keep all components on ice. Distribute 5.5 µL PCR cocktail into each well of a real‑time PCR plate, then add 4.5 µL of the corresponding diluted RT product. Mix by pipetting, briefly centrifuge the plate (~800 × g for a few seconds), seal, and place in the qPCR instrument. Run the following program: 50 °C 2 min (UDG), 95 °C 10 min (enzyme activation), then 40 cycles of 95 °C 15 sec + 60 °C 1 min. Analyze the data to obtain polysome‑associated mRNA distribution.
